open_obligations: Check whether prover-estimator debate needs a human-verifiable transcript to exist at all, or only an A-provable decomposition.
Check that completeness requires rho-stability, so the honest prover may not win on unstable problems.
Check that 'comparable efficiency' is relative to the prover class A, not polynomial time.
in.other_title: Prover-estimator debate mitigates the obfuscated arguments problem in recursive debate
in.rationale: Brown-Cohen, Irving and Piliouras ask whether an intermediate model exists where the honest prover always has an efficient strategy but the computation need not have a polynomial-length human-verifiable transcript, noting unbounded-prover debate runs into obfuscated arguments. Prover-estimator debate is proposed as a recursive protocol that, under certain stability assumptions, lets an honest debater win with a strategy requiring computational efficiency comparable to its opponent, mitigating the obfuscated arguments problem.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether an honest debater can have an efficient strategy without a polynomial-length human-verifiable transcript, in recursive debate with an oracle

text: The authors note that powerful AI systems may run polynomial-time computations with no polynomial-length human-verifiable transcript; the original unbounded-prover debate captures PSPACE, but with both provers unbounded it runs into the obfuscated argument problem, where a dishonest prover can in polynomial time produce an argument the honest prover needs exponential time to refute. They ask whether an intermediate model exists where the honest prover always has an efficient strategy but the computation need not have a polynomial-length human-verifiable transcript.
title: Open: beyond poly-length human-verifiable transcripts without obfuscated arguments
